MINUTES
  Special Meeting
  ALHAMBRA CITY COUNCIL
  Council Chambers, 111 South First Street

ROLL CALL: At 5:11 p.m., on Tuesday, July 14, 2026, the Alhambra City Council met in the
Council Chambers of Alhambra City Hall.

PRESENT:  MAZA, WANG, ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY
ABSENT:  LEE

Officials Present: City Manager Binnquist, Assistant City Manager Garcia, City Attorney Murphy,
Assistant City Clerk Lamb McCarthy, Director of Parks and Recreation Macias, Director of

CITY CLERK REPORT - NOTICE NO. N2M26-89

The Assistant City Clerk hereby reported that she duly gave notice of the special meeting of the
City Council being held this evening pursuant to the order of the Mayor and in accordance with
Section 54956 of the Government Code of the State of California.

  3) Jennifer Ng, via Zoom, noted transparency issues with the Special Meeting and stated

PRESENTATION

1.  SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA EDISON UPDATE – F2M26-27

  At the March 26 Strategic Plan session, the City Council requested a presentation from
  Southern California Edison (SCE). Areas where discussion was requested: A presentation
  of circuit maps with recent outage information, what type of claims can be filed for power
  loss expenses for residents, what SCE does to minimize business impacts for planned

   maintenance, and General Q & A. Jonathan HORTON, Government Relations Manager
  for SCE provided a presentation, which is on file in the City Clerk’s office.

  Discussion:  Councilmember WANG discussed the statistics on the slides and
  Mr. HORTON provided clarification regarding SAIDI or the average number of minutes of
  sustained power interruptions each year.

  Vice Mayor ANDRADE-STADLER discussed the response and concern from residents,
  requested more information as to providing outreach to residents who are not online, and
  further discussed the Northeast corner of District 5 with faulty circuits which could be a
  wildfire risk. Mr. HORTON provided a description of the circuits and made clarifications.
  Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER and Mr. HORTON went on to discuss recommended trees to
  be near power lines, financial assistance for senior citizens, and rebate programs for
  generators. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER noted that SCE should consider programs to offer
  generators to seniors.

  Councilmember WANG discussed various points in the presentation such as historic
  reliability of circuits serving Alhambra, outage causes for Alhambra, and the Capital
  Improvement map. Mr. HORTON provided clarification regarding Alhambra infrastructure,
  methods to report hazards and threats, and SCE’s plans to make improvements in
  Alhambra. Ms. WANG continued to discuss the uncertainty of outage times and the
  difficulties in planning for planned outages. She also suggested more information be
  available to seniors and medically vulnerable residents. She requested an annual report
  from SCE regarding service.

  Councilmember MAZA further discussed circuits in the Southwest part of the City and
  requested improvements there with a better schedule for implementation.

  Councilmember LEE discussed the Historical Reliability Chart in the presentation and
  requested more detail. Mr. HORTON provided clarification regarding SAIDI and SAIFI
  statistics. They went on to discuss the overview of circuits in Alhambra.

  Mayor MALONEY discussed Alhambra’s membership in the Clean Power Alliance and its
  ability to provide insight as a board member.

  Action Taken:  City Council received and order filed this informational report
  presented this evening.

2.  CHAMBER OF COMMERCE UPDATE – F2M21-43

  Alhambra Chamber of Commerce President, Mr. John BWARIE, presented an update for
  Chamber of Commerce activities. Mr. BWARIE discussed economic development,
  hospitality, outreach in other neighborhoods, and expressed support for the Economic
  Development Action Plan.

  Discussion:  Vice Mayor ANDRADE-STADLER and Mr. BWARIE discussed the
  former “Around Alhambra” local newspaper publication. Councilmember WANG
  discussed the need for diversity of businesses and specifically family friendly businesses.
  Councilmember MAZA also discussed the “Around Alhambra” publication and noted the
  challenging economic times for small businesses. Councilmember LEE and Mr. BWARIE
  discussed small businesses and outreach to family owned businesses.

3.  CONSIDERATION OF AND INTRODUCTION FOR FIRST READINGS OF ORDINANCE
  NO. O2M26-4867 AND ORDINANCE NO. O2M26-4868 CALLING AN ELECTION FOR
  A BALLOT MEASURE TO AMEND THE ALHAMBRA CHARTER PERTAINING TO
  TERM LIMITS AND A BALLOT MEASURE BANNING DATA CENTERS, INCLUDING
  ASSOCIATED CEQA DETERMINATION LANGUAGE FOR EACH – F2M26-33, O2M26-
  4867, O2M26-4868

  Mayor MALONEY provided an introduction for the item and provided background and
  clarifications regarding City process to adopt an ordinance. At the June 22, 2026 City
  Council meeting a member of the public submitted for Council’s consideration proposed
  language that could be used in two ballot measures for consideration by the voters in
  Alhambra. The first pertained to Council term limits and the second pertained to a ban on
  data centers. Council expressed interest in potentially holding a special meeting to
  discuss the two measures. The City Attorney’s office reviewed both measures, made
  some clarifying changes to the language to resolve certain ambiguities and drafted the
  ordinances necessary to place these on the ballot, should the Council wish to do so.

  The Alhambra Charter currently provides that a Councilmember may serve three
  consecutive four-year terms and then must take a three-year break before running again.
  At that point the Councilmember can serve another three consecutive terms before
  another break must be taken. This could be repeated indefinitely. The proposed language
  would limit a person from holding more than 5 Council terms during their lifetime. After the
  third consecutive term they must sit out one four-year term before running again, at which
  point they would be limited to two more consecutive terms. The language also was not
  intended to apply to terms served prior to 2027 by sitting Councilmembers. The proposed
  language has been modified to eliminate certain potential ambiguities that could arise in
  its implementation.

  On June 22, 2026, the City Council adopted Ordinance No. O2M26-4863 which included
  a ban on data centers. More specifically, the amendment includes a definition of data
  centers, and then lists them as prohibited in the employment zoning districts and does not
  list them as a permitted use in any other zone in the City. (Uses not listed as permitted are
  prohibited.) The proposed Ordinance would use the same definition used previously and
  add “Data Centers would be prohibited in all zones of the City” to the end of the definition.

  Mr. MALONEY noted receiving feedback from the public and that there was no community
  consensus regarding a charter amendment to amend Councilmember’s term limits. He
  stated that community expressed concerns in the perceived urgency of the ballot measure
  pertaining to term limits and that the majority of public urged Council review the subject in
  time. Mr. MALONEY stated that should the City decide to review term limits, that the review
  be conducted with time to receive appropriate input from staff and the public. He requested
  Council table discussion of the proposed ballot measure pertaining to Council term limits
  and stated that the public could still provide comment. Vice Mayor ANDRADE-STADLER
  supported Mr. Maloney’s suggestion and agreed that there could be future discussion of
  the topic. Council supported tabling consideration of a ballot measure pertaining to a
  Charter Amendment to change Council term limits at this time.

  Mr. MALONEY provided further clarification regarding the proposed Ballot Measure to ban
  data centers.

  Discussion:  Vice Mayor ANDRADE-STADLER highlighted Alhambra’s
  Environmental Sustainability goals and projects currently underway. She did not support
  a Data Center in Alhambra as a sustainable community. She discussed water as a human
  right and the plans to develop Alhambra’s industrial zones. She supported the proposed

   Councilmember WANG thanked speakers and staff for exploring different ideas. She
  spoke in support of a ballot measure to ban data centers and the vote of the people.

  Councilmember MAZA thanked the speakers and discussed the ordinance to ban data
  centers. He supported the ballot measure to ban data centers and motioned to approve

  Councilmember LEE also spoke against data centers in Alhambra and supported the

  Mayor MALONEY supported the ballot measure to ban data centers and discussed the
  need for environmentally sustainable practices.

  Action Taken:  City Council, by one motion, took the following actions:

  1.  Find the adoption of Ordinance No. O2M26-4868 pertaining to a ban on data
  centers in the City is not subject to further CEQA review as the City previously
  adopted a ban via City Council Ordinance No. O2M26-4863, for which CEQA
  review was undertaken and a CEQA determination was made. The proposed
  Ordinance No. O2M26-4868 would enact the same ban with no additional
  environmental impacts and as such is not a new project within the meaning of
  Public Resources Code Section 20165 and it can be seen with certainty that
  there will be no additional impacts not previously studied under CEQA Guidelines
  Section 15061(b)(3).

  2.  Declared introduced for its first reading:

  Ordinance No. O2M26-4868: An Ordinance of the Alhambra City Council
  providing for a General Municipal Election in Said City to be Held on

  Being Held for a Ballot Measure to Ban Data Centers within the City of
  Alhambra.

  3.  Directed staff to agendize for consideration at the July 27,2026 City Council
  meeting, the following items:

  a.  Second reading and adoption of the above-referenced ordinance;

  County of Los Angeles to order the consolidation of an Alhambra
  General Municipal Election to be held on November 3, 2026 with

  the same day.

4.  ADOPTION OF THE CITY OF ALHAMBRA ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT ACTION
  PLAN - F2M26-23, M2M26-116

  Economic Development Specialist MACCARLEY delivered a staff report. On April 24,
  2023, the City Council approved the 2023 Strategic Plan, which included Goal Three:
  Create a Strong Financial Base and a Strong Economic Base (Economic Development).
  One of the objectives of this goal was to develop an Economic Development Action Plan.
  The Plan would establish a comprehensive and integrated approach to economic
  development that strengthens the City’s economic base. On January 26, 2026, the draft
  Economic Development Action plan was presented to the City Council. The Council
  provided feedback focused on the inclusion of a vision for the Industrial Corridor. Council
  highlighted the on-going efforts to connect with the local colleges especially CalState LA
  and East Los Angeles College and the plan’s effort for encouraging additional
  development opportunities and growth on Valley Boulevard.

  Following the City Council meeting, Staff conducted public outreach on three separate
  occasions in the month of February 2026. Feedback from public outreach meetings have
  been incorporated in the Action Plan, which now included a vision for the Industrial
  Corridor. Updates were also made to the West Valley College District to more explicitly
  include residents. Overall, the Action Plan was well received and is ready to be adopted
  by the City Council. It would provide a strategic framework to guide the City’s economic
  growth and resilience over the next three to five years. The Plan reflects the community’s
  values, its collective vision for local economic resilience, and a shared understanding of a
  desired future.

  Public Comment:
  1) Bernice Ortega, also submitted comment via email, and requested Council table
  discussion to give the community more time to review, noting that the Plan may affect
  East Main Corridor and future developments. She also reported a faulty traffic signal
  at Granada St. and Main St.

  2) Rita Ledesma also submitted her comments via a letter to City Council. She expressed
  concerns regarding the West Valley College District and tying plans to CalState LA.
  She stated that the community wants the City to be family and pedestrian friendly, with
  open greenspace.

  Discussion:  Councilmember LEE spoke in support of the  Economic

  Councilmember MAZA spoke in support of the Plan. He addressed the concerns of the

5.  APPROVAL OF A CONTRACT FOR THIRD PARTY ADMINISTRATION OF WORKERS
  COMPENSATION CLAIMS – F2M18-42, C2M26-44, M2M26-117

  On July 1, 2018, the City Council authorized the City’s membership in the California Joint
  Powers Insurance Authority (CJPIA) for insurance services. Under the requirements for
  membership the City would be required to contract with a third-party administrator selected
  by CJPIA, Athens Administrators, to provide workers compensation claims administration
  services. The City’s Memorandum of Coverage for the Workers Compensation Program
  dictates that CJPIA, “at its discretion, will choose and manage service providers necessary
  to fulfill its objectives; including third party claims administrators, medical management
  providers, defense attorneys, investigators, etc.” The City previously contracted with
  Athens Administrators from 2023 to present and this agreement through June 30, 2029
  would constitute a continuation of services agreement as required by CJPIA.

  Discussion:  None.

  City manager or her designee to execute the contract and related documents; and,
  directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to execute the contract and finalize

6.  AUTHORIZE RFP: PYROTECHNIC SERVICES FOR THE ALHAMBRA FOURTH OF
  JULY CELEBRATION – F2M26-38, RFP2M26-9, M2M26-118

  The City of Alhambra sought to establish a 3-year contract with a professional pyrotechnic
  operator for the City’s Fourth of July Celebration. Although staff sought a 3-year contract,
  the City of Alhambra would have the option to renew the pyrotechnic services after each
  year, pursuant to satisfactory performance. At this time, staff recommended the City
  Council authorize the circulation of a Request for Proposals for pyrotechnic services. The
  Request for Proposals would be released on July 15, 2026.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council authorized staff to circulate a Request for Proposals to
  prospective operators to provide pyrotechnic services for the Alhambra Fourth of July
  Celebration, with proposals due by 4:40 p.m. on August 8, 2026; and, directed staff to
  undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M26-118)

  Vote:  Moved:  WANG  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  LEE, MAZA, WANG, ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

7.  RESOLUTION ADOPTING THE URBAN WATER MANAGEMENT PLAN AND WATER
  SHORTAGE CONTINGENCY PLAN – R2M26-22, F2M11-37, M2M26-119

  The California Department of Water Resources requires every urban water supplier to
  prepare and adopt an Urban Water management Plan (UWMP), including a Water
  Shortage Contingency Plan, and periodically update the Urban Water Management Plan
  at least once every five years, in years ending in six and one. The 2025 Urban Water
  Management Plan and Water Shortage Contingency Plan were prepared pursuant to the
  “Urban Water Management Planning Act” and the California Water Code and required
  adoption by July 2026. On June 22, 2026, City Council held a Public Hearing and adopted
  the Urban Water Management Plan, however, the approval was supposed to be done by
  resolution, so the required resolution was attached for Council adoption.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved Resolution R2M26-22 adopting the Urban
  Water Management Plan and Water Contingency Plan. (M2M26-119)

8.  NOTICE INVITING BIDS: CHILLED WATER SYSTEM UPGRADE AT THE ALHAMBRA
  POLICE DEPARTMENT – F2M26-39, N2M26-91

  On March 24, 2025, the City Council approved a one-year contract, commencing on April
  26, 2025, with Total Environmental Management Service, Inc. (TEM) for a temporary
  cooling unit at Alhambra Police Department due to a chiller failure resulting in no cooling
  in the building. Said contract was extended for another twelve months in order to
  accommodate the time needed to conduct the due diligence study of the current Heating,
  Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC) system in the building, prepare the
  specifications, obtain the necessary approvals from the Building Division, solicit bids, and
  start the construction. The consultant who prepared the HVAC design would also provide
  bid support and construction oversight to the project.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council authorized staff to issue notice inviting bids to
  prospective contractors for the Chilled Water System Upgrade at Alhambra Police
  Department, with bids due no later than 10:30 a.m. on Thursday, August 13, 2026 and
  opened at 11:00 a.m. that same day; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary
  to finalize the Council’s action.

  Vote:  Moved:  WANG  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  LEE, MAZA, WANG, ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

9.  QUARTERLY CONTRACTS REPORT AS OF JUNE 30, 2026 – F2M25-40

  On August 26, 2024, the City Council adopted Ordinance No. O2M24-4837, implementing
  the California Uniform Public Construction Cost Accounting Act (CUPCCAA), as outlined
  in California Public Contract Code Sections 22000–22045. On April 28, 2025, the City
  Council adopted Ordinance No. O2M25-4845, updating contract thresholds in accordance
  with recent CUPCCAA amendments. During this meeting, the Council also requested a
  report identifying all contracts awarded between $50,000 and $75,000, which previously
  required Council approval before CUPCCAA implementation. During the reporting period
  of April 1, 2026 through June 30, 2026, there were five contracts awarded in the amount
  of $50,000 to $75,000 without City Council approval.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council received and filed the quarterly contracts report for the
  period of April 1, 2026 through June 30, 2026.

  Vote:  Moved:  WANG  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  LEE, MAZA, WANG, ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY
